title: Staged precision handoff and zero-copy casting for attention kernels (INT8/FP8)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our attention kernels currently trigger an eager de-quantization pass when serving mixed-precision models. This creates extra memory copies and stalls on the critical path during both prefill and decode stages, increasing P95 latency and hurting throughput for short-turnaround requests. Goals: (1) eliminate unnecessary tensor copies during precision transitions, (2) provide a staged handoff that lets attention kernels accept mixed-precision inputs without materializing full FP32 buffers, and (3) retain numerical parity within acceptable bounds for customer workloads. Constraints: must work with existing KV cache layout, support streaming decode, and not regress peak throughput on Dedicated instances. This ticket implements a zero-copy casting adapter plus a staged precision handoff protocol that annotates tensors with 'precision views' and defers full upcasts until a kernel requires them. We will also add a small attention microkernel variant that operates primarily in INT8/FP8 + accumulation to FP16 to reduce upcast frequency.
acceptance_criteria: P50 decode latency no regression (<= baseline + 2ms) for 8-token requests on A100 80GB mixed workload
P95 latency improvement >= 8% on mixed-precision models compared to current main branch under 2000 rps
End-to-end token cost reduced by >= 6% due to fewer memory copies in staging benchmarks
No correctness regressions on our eval prompt set (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity within tolerance)
Unit and integration tests for precision views and zero-copy casting cover edge cases (sliced KV, cached prefixes)
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha: RFC posted to /docs/confluence/runtime/staged-precision-handoff. Initial microbenchmarks indicate 10-12% drop in memcpy time for small sequence lengths.
2025-02-22 - Marcus: Spike implemented a prototype that tags tensors with a view header. Verified zero-copy for contiguous KV append path; non-contiguous slices still require a copy (follow-up).
2025-02-25 - Eng review: agreed to keep fallback to eager upcast for rare shapes. Decision: add a lightweight profiler flag to track how often fallbacks occur in prod-mode Canary.
2025-02-27 - Design feedback (Lina Ramos): Ensure the kernel ABI change is backward-compatible; add version header to tensor view metadata.
notes: Implementation plan: (1) Add tensor view header and ABI flag (backwards compatible), (2) Implement zero-copy casting ops for contiguous tensors, (3) Add attention microkernel that consumes precision views and accumulates to FP16 where safe, (4) Integrate profiler flag and canary rollout, (5) Monitor fallbacks and iterate. Blockers: finalize kernel ABI with infra, and coordinate with Dedicated autoscaler team for large-scale perf runs. Follow-ups: non-contiguous slice optimization and autorouting policy that prefers precision-aware kernels at schedule-time.
